purpose: Every direct `.positions` read in src/, classified by the coordinate frame the reading site expects. Keyed by file plus enclosing symbol so the key survives edits above it. Enforced by scripts/lint-position-access.mjs; a read with no entry fails CI.

frames.source-local: The buffer as the loader wrote it, relative to the cloud's own sourceOrigin.
frames.project-local: Source-local plus the layer's Float64 sourceToProject translation, the shared project frame.
frames.render-local: Relative to a render origin picked for float precision: streaming node buffers, GPU uploads.
frames.world: Source-local plus sourceOrigin, in the file's own CRS.

Every read is the gather result from Viewer.gatherTerrainPositions, whose assembler folds each layer placement as it copies.
Each buffer is paired with its own sourceOrigin so the two epochs are gridded in one common world frame; differencing raw local coordinates would compare mismatched locations.
Both branches are gather output: the denser re-gather, or the space-export context that was itself copied from a gather.

The measure snap index is built from the active STATIC layer own buffer. Identity placement makes this equal to the project frame today; it is one of the consumers the fold must reach before multi-layer mounting is enabled.
The heuristic ground classifier scores a single layer against itself, so it works in that layer own frame.
Same single-layer classifier input as the derive path.
Reads only the buffer length to size a class array. The frame is still named because the length must match the layer this class array will be attached to.
Model internals: the cached min/max span is in the cloud own frame, and every caller adds sourceOrigin or a placement itself.
Model internals: the constructor validates and stores the buffer the loader produced, which is the definition of this cloud source frame.
Model internals: a length divided by three. Frame-independent, but the buffer it reads is the source-local one.
The project-frame accessor itself: source-local position plus the Float64 sourceToProject translation, computed at read time.
The world accessor itself: source-local position plus sourceOrigin, both fixed at construction.
The render-local accessor itself. This is the one place the label is attached to a streaming chunk buffer.
The source-local accessor itself. This is the one place the label is attached to a cloud buffer.

Numeric kernel. The grid is anchored on the buffer own bounds, so the result is invariant under a pure translation: static callers pass source-local, the streaming recolour passes render-local, and both are correct. What it must never be given is two frames concatenated.
Numeric kernel over one buffer. Static callers pass source-local and the streaming range seed passes render-local; the percentile band is meaningful in either, provided the buffer is all one frame.
Numeric kernel: slope shading from local gradients, which a translation cannot change. It is handed a single layer buffer in that layer own frame.
The patch provider returns the picked layer own neighbourhood buffer, and the patch is built around a point index in that same layer.
Numeric kernel: per-point spacing from nearest neighbours within one buffer, unchanged by a translation.
The Viewer hands it copyPlacedPositions output, so the polygon test runs against placed coordinates that match the screen the polygon was drawn on.

Two callers, two frames, both consistent with the projector they arrive with: the lasso volume walk passes copyPlacedPositions output with a plain camera projector, and the Viewer class edit passes the raw layer buffer with a projector that folds the placement itself. The invariant is that the points and the projector agree, not that the frame is fixed.
Receives the packed selection built from copyPlacedPositions, so the footprint and the reference plane are computed in the shared project frame.
assembleProfileBuffers folds each contributing layer placement while flattening, so the corridor walk reads project coordinates.
The stockpile input is the lasso selection, which is packed from placed positions.
Every caller (the Viewer volume sampler, the stockpile estimator, the lasso walk) supplies placed positions.
The photometric witness patch is a neighbourhood of one picked point inside one layer, taken from that layer own buffer; a tangent basis over neighbours is translation-invariant anyway.
Placement fold on the RAY, not the points: the ray drops into the layer source frame, the pick runs over the raw buffer, and the hit lifts back.
Streaming nodes are picked in the streaming render frame, which is where their decoded buffers and the ray both already are.
GPU upload boundary: the buffer goes to the mesh unchanged and the layer placement is applied at MESH level by setLayerPlacement, never written into the points.

The sampler callbacks registered here (profile, cut/fill volume, inspector patch) collect buffers from both sources: static layers contribute source-local buffers WITH their placement alongside, resident streaming nodes contribute render-local ones. Neither is lifted here; the assemblers fold placement as they copy.

The gather is the frame boundary itself: static layer buffers (source-local) and resident streaming node buffers (render-local) go IN with their placements, and sampleStridedTerrain folds each placement while striding, so the sample buffer that comes back out and is up-axis normalised is project-local.
The projector and the clip predicate add the layer placement offset themselves, so the raw layer buffer is the correct input; folding it again would place the layer twice.
Each epoch buffer is sampled and transformed together with its own origin, because a registration fit between two scans is only meaningful once both are in a common world frame.
The epoch buffer is lifted by its own origin before gridding, so both epochs land on the shared world grid.
The grid must span both epochs, so each buffer bounds are taken in world coordinates rather than in its own local frame.
Rebuilds a view over the transferred gather buffer, which the gather assembler already placed into the project frame.
